record.final_answer:
Short answer: I can't confirm it either way from this repo, and that's the important part of the answer — the decisive fact (what pardalo 4.2.0 retries) is not available here.

What the code does (client/charge.py:5-13)

  session = pardalo.Session(retry=Retry(total=3), timeout=10)
  session.post(".../v1/charges", json={order_id, amount_cents})

Two things make a double charge possible in principle:

1. If the retry layer resends POST after a connection error, then a request that was received and committed by billing but whose response was lost (drop or 10s read timeout) gets sent again. The body carries order_id, but nothing in this client marks the request as idempotent — whether a repeated order_id is rejected or creates a second charge is entirely the billing server's behaviour, and I have no evidence about that either.
2. Even if retries skip POST, create_charge raises and the caller can retry; same exposure, no idempotency key to protect it.

What I could not verify

  - pardalo is pinned at 4.2.0 (requirements.txt) but not installed here, not obtainable from PyPI, no wheel or lockfile anywhere on the box, and there's no vendored copy — so I cannot read the actual 4.2.0 Retry implementation.
  - The only prior evidence I had was a note on Pardalo 3.1 docs (read 2026-02-08) saying Retry(total=N) retries connection errors only for GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS and never POST or PATCH. Re-fetching that page today gives 404, and 3.1 is a major version behind 4.2.0, so it is a lead, not an answer. I've updated that note to record both the dead source and that 4.x is unestablished.

If the 3.1 rule still holds in 4.2.0, the retry policy cannot double-charge you — but note the 10s timeout still applies, and a POST that times out after delivery raises without any resend, leaving a charge you don't have a response for.

To settle it, one of these: install pardalo 4.2.0 and read Retry's method filter / Session.post, or ask the billing team whether POST is in the retry set. Either way, the durable fix is independent of the answer — send an Idempotency-Key header (or make order_id uniquely constrained server-side) so a duplicate POST is rejected. I haven't touched the file; say the word and I'll add the header.
